1.name: Auction Portal
description: Developing a web platform for online auctions connected to a Symfony backend.
Implementing key platform pages such as item detail, auction, and seller pages.
Building UI components in line with the project's design system, such as Badge, Tag, and Headline.
Developing a user zone with a sidebar, favorite items subpages, and account settings.
Designing and implementing skeleton loading states for smooth data fetching.
Fixing UI bugs and refining the responsive layout across the platform.

2.name: Component Library
description: Developing an internal shared React component library used across multiple projects.
Designing and implementing reusable components built on a design system.
Building complex components such as Select, MultiSelect, SubNavigation, and Badge.
Focus on type safety, accessibility, and documentation in Storybook.
Local testing of the library in a consuming application before publishing to npm.

3.name: E-commerce Platform
description: Developing a production B2C e-commerce platform connected to a Symfony backend.
Building UI for individual pages and components based on Figma designs.
Implementing key parts of the e-commerce functionality, including the shopping cart, discount module, and order gifts.
Creating a responsive mobile menu with multi-level category navigation.
Building the user account management UI, including multi-step forms.
Integrating REST APIs according to the OpenAPI specification using Kubb and TanStack Query.
Handling form implementation with React Hook Form and Zod.

1.name: Julian Xu
1.text: As Vendy’s mentor, I saw her exceed all my expectations. She learned React from scratch within the first month, something many people cannot achieve, and invested more than 100% in everything she did.

2.name: Karel Kutchan
2.text: I had the opportunity to lead Vendula and appreciated her responsible approach, attention to detail, and willingness to take feedback on board. I particularly valued her commitment to quality results and motivation to continue developing professionally.

1.name: Expo burza Pardubice
1.description: Website with information about a one-day event, coded using HTML and Sass. I used the Eleventy templating system to generate static pages. The project is the final work of the Become a Coder course.

2.name: Winery
2.description: Website with a wine catalog, where users can filter products and submit a reservation form. Built in JavaScript using Webpack for bundling. The catalog data is stored in a separate file as an array of objects. I worked on this project as part of the JavaScript 2 course.

3.name: Movie Database
3.description: Website with a movie database, allowing users to search and view movie details. I programmed the application in React and fetch data from a publicly available API. I developed this project as part of the ReactGirls Advent Coding Challenge in collaboration with Lenovo.

4.name: Words Game
4.description: English vocabulary practice app with a choice of 3 modules and the ability to change their default settings. I programmed the application in React and used Supabase for data management. This project was realized as part of the ReactGirls Mentoring Program.

5.name: Personal Website and Portfolio
5.description: Website showcasing my projects and skills. I initially refactored the static HTML/Tailwind CSS version into React with dynamic content. In the next phase, I added TypeScript to the existing project.

6.name: Superquiz
6.description: Quiz application with multiple-choice questions. I programmed the static HTML/CSS design in React with TypeScript and used Supabase for data management. I extended the original desktop version to be responsive for smaller devices.

7.name: XXXMuck
7.description: Simple e-shop with a product catalog. I fetch data from an API. Each product has its own detailed page with an interaction button. I styled the application using Tailwind CSS and daisyUI. For dark/light mode switching, I used the NextUI library.

1.name: How to Web
1.description: I refreshed the basics of HTML and CSS in a fictional project. I learned to use Developer tools, render SVG icons via sprite technique, build responsive layouts across devices using flexbox and organize CSS with Sass by splitting code into smaller parts.

2.name: Become a Coder
2.description: Learned to create responsive pages, use advanced layout techniques – flexbox and CSS grid, organize CSS with the Sass preprocessor and split code into smaller parts, and create site content using the Eleventy static site generator with templates.

3.name: JavaScript 1
3.description: Basics of programming, DOM manipulation, use event principles and respond to user input, and work with media on the page. Capable of creating a simple application and subsequently publishing it through my GitHub account.

4.name: JavaScript 2
4.description: Mastered the basics of creating frontend applications in pure JavaScript. Practical knowledge of communicating with REST APIs. I can use basic building blocks such as components, authentication, and client-side routing. Capable of creating projects based on Webpack.

5.name: ReactGirls Mentoring Program
5.description: Programming my own project, where I advanced my skills in developing applications in React. During the project, I had an assigned mentor who provided valuable advice and regularly conducted code reviews.

6.name: React 1 - Basics
6.description: Refreshed the basics of JavaScript and ES6+ syntax. Understanding of the fundamental principles of React. I can create a simple application composed of components that fetch data from an API, and work with useState, useEffect, and React Router.

7.name: Basics of TypeScript
7.description: I mastered the basics of TypeScript and its type system, simple data modeling, project setup in TypeScript including bundling, basics of parametric types (generics), and recommended practices for developing web applications in TypeScript and React.

8.name: React 2 - Tools and Techniques
8.description: Mastered using TypeScript in React applications. I gained a deeper understanding of React and the component lifecycle and learned to create custom hooks and advanced state management methods using useContext. I can handle forms and validate data using Formik. I became familiar with writing unit tests and testing through Vitest.

9.name: Basics of Next.js
9.description: Creating multi-page applications using the Pages Router and dynamic segments in the URL. Styling methods: CSS/Sass, Styled Components, Tailwind CSS, CSS-in-JS. Data rendering and fetching: getServerSideProps (SSR), getStaticPaths (SSG), Automatic Static Optimization. Image optimization. Awareness of full-stack application development through API Routes and authentication setup.

10.name: Figma
10.description: Familiarized myself with the Figma environment and its basic features. I understand text styling, adding colors and shadow effects to elements. Work with auto layout for efficient element arrangement. I create components and their variants, design wireframes and functional prototypes according to specifications. Using Figma Variables for clear style management across the design.

11.name: Figma Advanced
11.description: I expanded my knowledge of responsive design principles and designing interfaces for different breakpoints. I utilized Figma Variables to maintain consistency across the project and to organize styles clearly. I mastered the principles of microinteractions and their importance for UX, enabling me to design functional and user-friendly interfaces.

12.name: React Academy
12.description: Focus on developing applications in React and TypeScript, working with component architecture, state management, forms, and communication with REST API. It also included working with Git for code versioning and team collaboration on joint projects.

description: Managing and creating web content: product listing, data updates, marketing support.
